articles.title: Un gol de Víctor Muñoz lidera la remontada del Liverpool en Brentford
articles.standfirst: Los de Iraola, rivales del Villarreal, sufrieron las lesiones de Szoboszlai y Frimpong
articles.summary: La expulsión de Yarmoliuk 'facilitó' la victoria de los de Iraola... con un gran tanto del español
articles.body: El Liverpool, poco a poco, comienza a curar las heridas que le dejó la derrota ante el Manchester City (0-3). Los de Andoni Iraola, rivales del Villarreal, golearon al LASK Linz (3-6) en Champions y han ganado, remontando, al Brentford (1-2), con un gol de Víctor Muñoz, para situarse quintos con 12 puntos, a nueve de los de Maresca, líderes. Fue un triunfo sufrido. Y eso que el Brentford acabó con nueve por las expulsiones de Yarmoliuk (45') y Janelt (92'). Empezó, eso sí, perdonando. Barcola desperdició un mano a mano en el 20' -remató fuera- tras una gran presión de Víctor Muñoz, titular. Acto seguido, en el 23', el internacional español, dio el susto. Se llevó la mano a la rodilla tras una mal gesto en un lance con Lewis-Potter y tuvo que ser atendido. Por suerte, todo quedó en un susto y pudo seguir jugando. El que se tuvo que retirar, en el 32', fue Dominik Szoboszlai. El húngaro, que volvía de lesión, dejó su lugar a Nyoni. De un posible penalti de Ouattara sobre Mac Allister en el 41'... se pasó al 1-0 del Brentford en el 44'. Centró al área Igor Thiago y cabeceó a la red Lewis-Potter llegando desde atrás, libre de marca. Golazo. De pronto, el Brentford sufrió un duro revés. Yarmoliuk vio la roja en el añadido por propinar un cabezazo sin balón a Jacquet. La expulsión dio alas al Liverpool, que perdió a Frimpong por lesión en el 52'. Sin embargo, Kelleher, ex de los 'reds', les negó el empate en el 59' con un paradón a disparo lejano de Mac Allister. Nada pudo hacer, sin embargo, para evitar el 1-1 de Víctor Muñoz en el 62'. El ex de Osasuna recibió en largo de Wirtz y, tras una cabalgada 'marca de la casa', recortó de tacón con la diestra para 'sentar' a Lewis-Potter y marcó con un sutil disparo al palo largo. Dos goles y una asistencia suma ya en Premier el excanterano del Real Madrid. No se hizo esperar el definitivo 1-2. Llegó en el 70'. Centró Mac Allister, cedió atrás Barcola y marcó Isak con una bonita maniobra: controló con la derecha y fusiló con la izquierda. El larguero, ya en el 79', impidió que Barcola ampliara distancias en un final de partido que dejó una nueva expulsión para el Brentford. Janelt vio la roja en el 92'. El Liverpool de Iraola vuelve a la senda del triunfo.

articles.title: Aberdeen 3-1 St Mirren: Brad Lyons, Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua score as Dons win and leapfrog opponents in table
articles.summary: Report as goals from Brad Lyons, Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua help Aberdeen secure a 3-1 victory at home to St Mirren; Eseosa Sule brought the away side level but Aberdeen were too strong for St Mirren in the second half
articles.body:
Brad Lyons gave the hosts the lead in spectacular fashion after just two minutes, but the Buddies went on to dominate the first half and levelled through Eseosa Sule.

A much-improved second-half display saw strikes from Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua earn the Dons three points.

Lyons opened the scoring when he drove forward from Conor Ronan's pass and unleashed a spectacular 22-yard effort into the top corner, clipping the crossbar on the way in.

Dons goalkeeper Marius Muller had to be alert to save from Killian Phillips after a Declan John cutback, with Mats Knoester sliding in to block the former Aberdeen loanee's rebound effort.

A Luke Thomas cross saw Muller save again from Sule's header, before Aberdeen finally showed signs of growing back into the game - Nisbet was presented with two headed opportunities in the space of three minutes.

But St Mirren were the more dangerous, and while Muller once again denied Phillips from a curling effort, Saints were level three minutes before the break.

Marcus Fraser's superb switch to the far side saw Thomas hold the ball up for Phillips, whose cut-back was swept home at the far post by Sule.

Aberdeen made two substitutions and a change of formation at the break as they looked to gain a foothold, with Tony Yogane flashing an effort over the crossbar before fellow replacement Stuart Armstrong saw an effort ruled out for offside.

But they were back in front before the hour.

Paul Nsio hauled down Yogane on the edge of the area, and although referee John Beaton initially awarded a free-kick, a VAR review upgraded the call to a penalty.

Nisbet's initial effort was weak and well saved by Jacob Chapman, but the goalkeeper could not hold on to the ball and the Dons captain drilled home at the second attempt.

They extended their lead after 72 minutes as Mouloua, barely on the park for 60 seconds, latched onto Afeez Aremu's quick free-kick to beat the St Mirren line and curl the ball into the bottom-right corner.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Sigue el fuego cruzado y Tebas responde ahora a Uribes: "Desde la presidencia del CSD cabe esperar rigor, imparcialidad y coherencia"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de LaLiga reacciona a las presidente del CSD
articles.summary: El presidente de LaLiga reacciona a las presidente del CSD
articles.body: El fuego cruzado a varias bandas no cesa. Javier Tebas, presidente de LaLiga, acaba de responder a José Manuel Rodríguez Uribes. El presidente del CSD había cargado con dureza tras comparar Tebas los métodos empleados por el Real Madrid con los de Goebbels en la Alemania del III Reich. Esta es la resuesta de Tebas: Señor Rodríguez Uribes: Ayer manifesté que no daba crédito a las informaciones sobre una posible actuación del CSD por mis declaraciones. Tras escuchar hoy sus palabras y su petición de disculpas al Real Madrid, considero necesario hacer algunas precisiones. Le adjunto dos post del ministro Óscar Puente: la del 23 de septiembre de 2025, referida a Telemadrid, y otra sobre un mensaje de Jorge Buxadé fechado el 29 de julio de 2026. Acompaño también dos declaraciones de Patxi López, portavoz socialista en el Congreso: su respuesta en la entrevista con HuffPost del 29 de marzo de 2025 y sus declaraciones del 19 de septiembre de 2026, recogidas por 101TV. Las cuatro imágenes permiten leer sus palabras y comprobar el uso que hacen de las referencias a Goebbels. Estos no son los únicos precedentes. Dispongo de más declaraciones de responsables públicos en el mismo sentido. Usted ha subrayado la responsabilidad institucional de mi cargo. Comparto que esa responsabilidad debe tenerse presente. También corresponde tenerla presente cuando se valoran las palabras de un ministro del Gobierno o del portavoz de un grupo parlamentario. Peronen mis palabras hay una diferencia, dejé expresamente escrito: "La comparación es con esas técnicas de propaganda, no con una ideología ni, por supuesto, con la afición madridista". Mi crítica se refería a la repetición sistemática, la selección interesada de hechos y la construcción de un enemigo. Esa delimitación debe formar parte de cualquier valoración rigurosa de lo que dije. Puede discrepar de mi análisis y de la referencia utilizada. Pero afirmar que queda fuera de la libertad de expresión exige una fundamentación que atienda al contenido completo y al contexto. Y cualquier eventual actuación disciplinaria necesita, además, una base jurídica concreta. Desde la presidencia del CSD cabe esperar rigor, imparcialidad y coherencia. La responsabilidad institucional exige un criterio consistente, con independencia de quién formule la crítica y de quién la reciba.

articles.title: Birmingham 3-0 QPR: Liam Millar scores twice in win for in-form Blues
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Birmingham City and Queens Park Rangers at St Andrew's on Saturday; Liam Millar scores twice as Chris Davies’ Blues maintain their fine recent form with a comfortable win.
articles.body:
In front of watching chairman Tom Wagner, Millar netted to swing the game Birmingham's way in the 27th minute and then doubled their advantage just after the break.

On both occasions he was assisted by Tomoki Iwata while Demarai Gray added the gloss in the first minute of stoppage time by hammering a pull-back by fellow substitute Luis Vazquez into the top corner as Birmingham confirmed a statement victory.

The visitors made a confident start and might have gone ahead from Paul Smyth's seventh-minute long throw.

The ball eluded Birmingham's backline and fell to Boy Kemper, but he was falling away on the stretch as he diverted it just wide from close range.

Birmingham had a huge shout for a penalty in the 18th minute after slicing through QPR down the right.

Kemper slid in to stop a pass reaching Bright Osayi-Samuel and succeeded in only scooping the ball back into the heart of the area.

As it bounced about amid a crowd of bodies, August Priske blasted a shot on the turn that struck the underside of Ronnie Edwards' upraised left arm as he tried to block.

Presumably the referee Thomas Kirk felt Edwards was in too close proximity for it to be avoidable.

There was joy, though, for the home side nine minutes later when they took the lead after a fast break from QPR's first corner of the match.

Jay Stansfield hassled Rayan Kolli out of possession not far from Birmingham's penalty area and as Kealey Adamson attempted to help, QPR got in a muddle.

Stansfield moved the ball onto Iwata and he slipped Millar clean through at halfway. The Canada international kept his composure to surge on and sidefoot a low shot past Pierce Charles at his near post, from the left of the area.

Three minutes before the break Kwame Poku fed Kolli down the right channel and he hit a powerful attempt at goal only for James Beadle, on his 50th appearance for Birmingham, to stand strong and beat it away.

Birmingham and doubled their advantage in the 49th minute, dispossessing QPR in midfield through Iwata and then teeing up Millar to finish.

After picking the pocket of Glen Kamara, Iwata advanced to the edge of the area and received a return pass from Patrick Roberts before rolling the ball into the path of Millar, coming in off the left. Millar swept the ball firmly first time past Charles from 10 yards to put clear daylight between the teams.

The R's refused to lay down however as they then stepped up efforts to try and retrieve the situation.

Beadle made an important, sprawling save to kept out a powerful sidefooter from Edwards from the angle of the area in the 63rd minute.

Millar came close to a hat-trick sooner after when Birmingham caused panic from a cross by substitute Carlos Vicente. The ball was flicked clear but only as far as Millar who thumped the ball fiercely on the volley but straight at a grateful Charles.

In the 69th minute the game exploded into controversy when Birmingham captain Christoph Klarer dribbled the ball out of defence and then overran it on his second touch. He slid in as Jimmy Dunne nicked it away and caught the R's skipper on the foot. Dunne writhed and rolled around in agony and once order was restored referee Kirk gave Klarer a talking-to and showed a yellow card.

As the clock ticked over to 90 minute plus one, the Blues capitalised as QPR pushed forward. Stansfield worked the ball to Vazquez on the right of the area and he laid it back for Gray to thump in from close range.

"He's doing great. I've said before I've tried to get him every year to the club and I finally convinced him.

"He has been super. He has got energy. He has got intelligence. He has got quality. And when you get a chance and can be clinical with it, then you're a really good winger. It was a super performance.

"With players it is hard to predict how they do whether on loan or if you sign them. Do they fit? Do they settle in? He looks like he's made for this place. We love having him here, he seems to love being here and that's a good combination."

"The goals were more our fault than their quality.

"We had the first big opportunity in the opening 15-20 minutes. We score this and it changes the face of the game.

"The way we conceded the goals was very, very unusual.

"The first one was from our corner. They were 90 metres away. It was a lack of maturity in this situation.

"And then to concede immediately after half-time. I don't want to talk about the referee's decision, it was more from our situation."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Derby 0-1 Stoke: Luke Graham nets winner for Potters
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Derby County and Stoke City at Pride Park on Saturday; Luke Graham scores the only goal in a narrow victory for the Potters at the struggling Rams.
articles.body:
The Scotland defender headed in a free-kick early in the second half and that was enough to settle a scrappy contest.

Derby, who are missing a number of key players, battled away and nearly snatched a point when David Ozoh's shot was superbly saved by goalkeeper Viktor Johansson.

The win keeps Stoke in the top eight and leaves Derby in the bottom three still searching for a first home win of an increasingly difficult season.

Stoke had the first chance of a sunny but chilly afternoon when Lamine Cisse broke forward and pulled the ball to Jack McGlynn but his low shot lacked the power to trouble Josh Vickers.

Carlton Morris looked to have got away from Bosun Lawal who appeared to trip the Derby striker but referee Oliver Langford waved away protests.

The game became increasingly scrappy but the Rams ended the first half with a corner that fell to Sammie Szmodics but his goalbound shot was blocked by a defender.

Stoke had failed to build on a promising start and had been guilty of giving the ball away, so boss Mark Robins would have been expecting a big improvement in the second half.

His players responded by taking the lead in the 49th minute through Graham who met Ethan Galbraith's free-kick with a header that Vickers got a hand to but the ball went in off his left post.

Derby responded with Ozoh getting the better of Lawal but he hesitated and his shot was blocked.

They had another chance in the 63rd minute when Rhian Brewster shot narrowly wide from the edge of the area and for the first time in the match, Derby were putting Stoke under pressure.

But the visitors almost got a second on the break in the 84th minute with Ben Johnson sliding a pass across to Justin Devenny who could not get a strong enough contact on his shot.

It nearly proved costly because Derby were denied an equaliser by a brilliant save from Johansson who plunged to his right to keep out Ozoh's low drive in the 89th minute.

"We asked for a reaction after Wednesday's first 45 minutes and we certainly got that.

"I was very proud of the effort of the group today, we battled against a very good team and limited them to next to nothing. We created some decent chances ourselves, so to lose the game is frustrating.

"It is what it is at the moment, we're not getting much luck. It's a frustrating period for us but this is the Championship, teams go through periods like this and I think we've got a valid reason why it's been difficult.

"We've got six or seven starters (missing) who would come into the team and make us stronger, but with the effort of the group up to now we could easily have got a couple more wins so it's important we keep believing in the process.

"The injuries haven't helped, we're going through a difficult period but we'll come through it. Also, it's my job to win games, there's no excuses. My head's on the door and I understand we haven't won enough games at the moment and it's my responsibility."

"We gave the ball away too often and in one or two areas we looked tired but we dug out another three points.

"They threw everything at us but we defended really well, we got blocks in, we stopped crosses and broke things up and started counter-attacks, but we gave the ball away too cheaply in really poor areas which gave them momentum, hope and belief.

"It wasn't a game for the purists by any stretch of the imagination, but it was one that you can learn an awful lot from and an awful lot about your players.

"I think we'd have gone under last year but we didn't, we found the resilience to see the game out and that was really pleasing on the back of a three-game week. You can't underestimate how difficult that is."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Swindon 1-1 Walsall
articles.summary: Tai Sodje's second-half leveller maintained Walsall's unbeaten record in a 1-1 draw against a much-improved Swindon side.
articles.body:
Town went ahead in the softest fashion after just five minutes from a long Mitch Clark throw which saw Stephan Negru hook the ball to Aaron Drinan to poke in from two yards out.

Joseph Hungbo then slipped in the unmarked Antwoine Hackford who launched well over before Clark ran 20 yards to pick up a loose ball and blast at the Saddlers keeper.

Billy Kirman found Negru in a crowded box but his hook drifted over.

Sodje rampaged down the right and hit a vicious dipping shot but Connor Ripley pulled off a stunning save to claw it away.

He then denied Mason Hancock at the near post.

Walsall drew level in the 54th minute when Sodje nodded home a looping deflection at the back post after Ripley had done well to keep out a Hancock piledriver with one hand.

Drinan then thundered just wide of the post.

Ripley did well to repel a hard shot on the turn from Aaron Pressley but neither side could break the deadlock.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Man City 3-2 Ipswich: Erling Haaland's incredible scoring run continues as Enzo Maresca's side continue to weather storm
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Man City stayed perfect in the Premier League by earning their seventh win; Erling Haaland scored twice and was denied his hat-trick by VAR; Ipswich were valiant in defeat, battling until the end and giving City a fright late on
articles.body:
Banana-crazed fans, a tradition that started in the 1980s, made for a playful atmosphere, and City's players responded with another demonstration of dogged defiance to move six points clear at the top. Their focus on winning football matches despite the huge scrutiny the club is under cannot be questioned.

Pep Guardiola was the guest of honour when PSG visited in the week. On Saturday, it was former director Txiki Begiristain, who oversaw an unprecedented period of domestic dominance during his time at the Etihad. City are maintaining a united front wherever possible.

Erling Haaland's appetite for scoring goals remains unaffected, netting in each half to take his seasonal tally to 12. He's scored four just this week - and is now the fastest of any player in Premier League history to reach 100 non-penalty goals. VAR cruelly denied him a hat-trick late on, too.

It was the forgotten Phil Foden who edged City ahead, scoring for the first time since December 2025 to end his 23-game run without a goal. Jeremy Doku's trickery gave him the opportunity to beat Christian Walton with a guided low finish and he made it look easy.

And although Daizen Maeda had battling Ipswich level within 155 seconds of Foden's strike, they had no answer for the quality of Haaland. "He's not just scoring," raved Enzo Maresca afterwards, "he's a leader, a captain. He's doing very well."

Mateo Kovacic teed up an easy first for the striker to head home in the first half and Iliman Ndiaye slid him through for a well-taken second in the second. City were cruising, but a jittery finish has become customary at the Etihad and after Zian Flemming made the scoreline 3-2 from the penalty spot, nerves jangled.

But it would seem that nothing was going to stand in the way of Maresca becoming the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club. With City fighting against the re-write of their recent history, that is one achievement that cannot be stripped away.

19: GOAL! Doku picks out Foden to score a smart opener on his return to the starting XI.

21: GOAL! Ipswich respond immediately as Maeda shrugs off Marc Guehi far too easily and beats Gianluigi Donnarumma with a low finish.

34: GOAL! Kovacic glides down the righthand side of the box unopposed, before clipping a lovely ball for Haaland to head on the penalty spot.

56: MISS! Nico O'Reilly misses a golden opportunity to make the scoreline more comfortable but skews his header off target.

68: GOAL! Haaland steps onto a brilliant pass from Ndiaye and slots past Walton.

85: VAR! Haaland thinks he's completed his hat-trick before VAR rule Enzo Fernandez offside in the build up.

88: PENALTY! VAR awards Ipswich a penalty after Guehi makes contact with Abdul Fatawu inside the box. Flemming buries the spot-kick.

Erling Haaland limped down the tunnel immediately after the full-time whistle. But Man City boss Enzo Maresca believes his star striker has not suffered anything serious.

"Unfortunately, in 10 minutes, we had four or five players [with injury issues]. Kovacic, Erling, Antoine and Nico. They are inside now. We will see.

On Haaland : "I don't know. I ask him, he said he was ok. Nothing serious. The only one we need to wait a little bit is Antoine, so we will see."

O'Neil confident Ipswich can continue to compete in PL

"Really disappointed. I did believe we could take points. I'm proud of what the players gave. It takes a lot to come here and keep yourself in the game. This is an incredible group, they gave everything for 102 minutes. It's a privilege to represent them.

"The second goal against us is what really annoys me. We'd worked on that a lot. And then maybe some quality in the final third, we weren't quite good enough in those moments. It just meant we fell a bit short. We've still shown everyone we can compete."

Asked if it feels any different to be playing Man City against the backdrop of their case with the Premier League, O'Neil added : "No. It's just us against City. Trying to win. Bananas or no bananas. It makes no difference to me."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Safonov sostiene a un PSG de dos partes al que le va más la Champions
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Luis Enrique se vuelve a tambalear en la liga pero remonta un partido gracias a la exhibición del portero ruso antes del encuentro contra el Barcelona
articles.summary: El equipo de Luis Enrique se vuelve a tambalear en la liga pero remonta un partido gracias a la exhibición del portero ruso antes del encuentro contra el Barcelona
articles.body: Si algo queda claro de este inicio de temporada es que al PSG le va más jugar en Europa que en su país. O al menos, se siente más cómodo. En medio de la exhibición que el equipo de Luis Enrique dio hace sólo tres días en Manchester en Champions League, y con el encuentro ante el Barcelona en el horizonte, al conjunto parisino se le volvió a hacer bola un nuevo partido en la Ligue 1 en su visita a Estrasburgo. Y para muestra, las masivas rotaciones que volvieron a hacer un equipo más previsible y con poco vértigo en ataque. El equipo local arrancó muy fuerte con un par de disparos que se marcharon por encima del larguero, lo que hacía presuponer otra complicada jornada para los parisinos en la liga doméstica. Sin embargo, poco después el equipo de Luis Enrique se hizo con el balón y tuvo tres ocasiones muy claras para ponerse por delante. Jörgensen tapó un cabezazo de Ferran mientras que Akliouche y Lucas Hernández perdonaron con toda la portería para ellos. Sin embargo, un despiste en la defensa permitió al Strasbourg marcar el primero del partido. Al cuarto de hora, Gio Reyna se metió en el área y su disparo tocó ligeramente en Lucas para despistar y batir a Safonov. A partir de ahí, mucho balón del PSG pero nada de peligro, que volvió a notar las siete modificaciones respecto al partido de Copa de Europa contra el Manchester City. Luis Enrique no realizó ninguna sustitución tras el paso por vestuarios, y el ritmo siguió siendo el mismo. De hecho, Safonov salvó a los suyos con una tremenda mano abajo a un remate de cabeza de Harder, que se elevó por encima de la defensa. Sólo tardó ocho minutos el técnico español en alterar su plan y dar entrada en el campo a Nuno Mendes, Vitinha y Doué. Fue entonces cuando llegaron los peores momentos del PSG. Tras el ingreso de Achraf y Dembélé, el Strasbourg apretó con cuatro tiros a puerta en dos minutos que salvó Safonov como pudo. El meta ruso sostuvo a su equipo y apenas en la siguiente jugada se encontró con un penalti revisado por el VAR. Pero parecía que hoy no iba a ser la tarde de los parisinos. Dembélé falló desde los once metros, en lo que supone el tercer error consecutivo del PSG tras los desaciertos anteriores de Doué y Ferran Torres, y los locales achicaban agua como podían. No obstante, quince minutos de presión fueron suficientes para el todopoderoso equipo visitante. Zabarnyi abría la lata para los suyos tras encontrarse completamente sólo en el área pequeña después de un centro del propio Dembélé, en uno de los pocos errores del Strasbourg en el partido, que desde ahí no podía salir de su área. El Balón de Oro fue protagonista en los pocos minutos que estuvo en el campo, ya que en el minuto 85 recortaba en la frontal del área para fusilar a Jörgensen y poner a su equipo por delante. Pero el sofoco no terminaría ahí para el PSG, que tuvo que defender los últimos minutos con un jugador menos por la lesión de Nuno Mendes. Luis Enrique no tenía más cambios y tocaba aguantar como fuera, más aún tras las molestias de Akliouche tras una dura entrada al tobillo que les hizo defender con nueve. Pero un balón en largo de Safonov en la última del partido lo pinchó Dembélé, que se la cedió a Ferran y el español le regaló el definitivo a Doué. El PSG salva otra bala en la liga doméstica y se prepara para la batalla del martes ante el Barcelona.

articles.title: Logan Costa: “Estanos tristes y nos sabe a poco este punto”
articles.standfirst: El central caboverdiano disfrutó de su segunda titularidad esta temporada
articles.summary: El central caboverdiano disfrutó de su segunda titularidad esta temporada
articles.body: Logan Costa sigue acumulando minutos tras vivir una temporada tan complicada como fue la pasada a causa de una grave lesión. El defensa de origen africano fue titular ante el Elche y acabó con sensaciones agridulces: feliz por sentirse cada vez más integrado en el grupo y amargado por un empate con sabor claro a derrota. “Nos sabe a poco, estamos un poco tristes pero también es verdad que hay muchas cosas buenas en un partido como este. No nos llevamos los tres puntos pero sobre esta base podemos trabajar bien para seguir ganando y conseguirlo en los próximos partidos. Sólo nos faltó el gol, pero al menos no encajamos. Ya tenemos que quedarnos con eso y que es un punto que hay que hacerlo bueno en el futuro”, afirmó tras el duelo de su equipo ante el cuadro ilicitano. El caboverdiano reconoció , eso sí, que la puntuación liguera de su equipo está por debajo de las expectativas generadas: “Este equipo quiere estar arriba, ganar todos los partidos y durante la semana se trabaja para eso. Por eso nos deja mal no hacerlo como hoy. En lo particular estoy contento por jugar, pero lo que de verdad quería es la victoria. De todas formas es verdad que me hacen falta minutos y acumular 90 más en las piernas me hace feliz". De la misma forma el defensa se refirió al partido que su equipo disputará el próximo martes en cancha del Liverpool, asegurando que van “sin miedo”: “No es la primera vez que voy a Anfield, es un gran campo. Pero no deja de ser un estadio de fútbol, como lo son otros, y con esa mentalidad tenemos que ir. Podemos competir contra cada equipo y es lo que vamos a hacer el próximo martes”.

images.caption: Logan Costa, jugador del Villarreal VILLARREAL CF

articles.title: In 2026, Gerard Piqué joined India’s FYERS American Gambits after backing Freestyle Chess a year earlier: How the Barcelona legend is building his chess business empire
articles.summary: Explore how soccer legend Gerard Piqué is revolutionizing chess through his investments in Freestyle Chess and FYERS American Gambits, and his vision for a global chess empire.
articles.body: Gerard Piqué had spent years looking for ways to make sport work differently, even before he retired from football in 2022. Last year, that interest took him into chess, where he invested in Freestyle Chess; in August 2026, he added another stake by joining the FYERS American Gambits as a strategic shareholder. The move brought the former Barcelona defender into a growing business around elite chess, digital audiences, and sporting entertainment, inserting his venture directly into the Tech Mahindra-backed Global Chess League, where the Indian-based franchise competes on a global stage.Piqué’s chess investment followed a career built around sporting venturesPiqué retired in 2022 after making 615 official appearances for Barcelona and winning 30 trophies with the club, including three Champions League titles. He also helped Spain win the 2010 World Cup, but his business ambitions had taken shape while he was still playing.In 2017, he founded Kosmos, a sports, media and entertainment company focused on developing new sporting properties and business models. Kosmos later created the Kings League, a seven-a-side football competition featuring shorter matches, unconventional rules, streamers and content creators, with a format designed for digital audiences.Piqué’s interest in chess became public in 2025 through his investment in Freestyle Chess, a venture founded by grandmaster Magnus Carlsen and German entrepreneur Jan Henric Buettner. In July that year, Piqué attended the Freestyle Chess Grand Slam in Las Vegas, where he joined a broadcast with grandmaster David Howell, international master Tania Sachdev and Buettner. He said it was his first top-level chess event.Asked about his favourite player, Piqué answered: “For me, Magnus. I think for everyone. He is a legend.” When asked where Carlsen might play on a football pitch, Piqué joked: “I assume in the midfield because he will move the team all around!”He joined FYERS American Gambits as a strategic shareholderOn 17 August 2026, the FYERS American Gambits announced Gerard Piqué’s entry as a strategic shareholder at a press conference in Bengaluru. The Indian-owned professional chess franchise, which is backed by the online stock brokerage firm FYERS, stated that his involvement reflects their ambition to drive the global growth of the sport.Piqué joins an established ownership group that includes Indian cricket star Ravichandran Ashwin, a co-owner since the team’s debut in 2024. The Gambits compete in the Global Chess League, a groundbreaking tournament launched by Tech Mahindra and FIDE. As the world's first franchise-based chess league, it features six international teams competing in a fast-paced, digital-first format. The team’s CEO and co-owner, Prachura P P, described the investment as a landmark moment that perfectly bridges Indian corporate backing with international sports entertainment.“Gerard understands what it takes to build a global sporting property, one that combines elite competition with compelling storytelling, passionate communities and a strong connection with fans,” Prachura said. He added that Piqué’s belief in the franchise’s vision was meaningful as it worked towards building “the future of chess”.The financial terms of Piqué’s investment, including the size of his stake, were not disclosed. His role was presented as a strategic investment rather than a public endorsement, although the franchise did not detail the precise commercial arrangements.Piqué’s investment arrived as chess pursued wider audiencesThe Global Chess League is the competition; FYERS American Gambits is one of its franchises, with FYERS serving as the team’s title sponsor. Piqué’s involvement fits his wider interest in turning established sports into entertainment properties that can reach audiences beyond their traditional fan bases.Freestyle Chess and the Global Chess League approach that ambition differently, but both seek to package elite chess for broader audiences. Piqué’s experience building the Kings League gives him a familiar perspective on digital presentation, fan communities and sports storytelling.He was also part of a growing group of high-profile athletes investing in chess. In March 2026, Manchester City forward Erling Haaland’s investment in the FIDE-approved Total Chess World Championship Tour was reported. The tour is organised by the team behind Norway Chess, which later announced a $10 million funding round featuring Norwegian cross-country skiing star Johannes Høsflot Klæbo, former cycling world champion Thor Hushovd and business investors.American Gambits finished third in Piqué’s first seasonPiqué joined the franchise shortly before the fourth season of the Global Chess League, held in Bengaluru from 3 September to 13 September 2026. FYERS American Gambits finished third, securing a podium place behind champions Ganges Grandmasters and runners-up Alpine APL Pipers.The reported season prize fund totalled $1 million, distributed through team standings, game points and a champions’ bonus. The standings-based payouts listed $250,000 for Ganges Grandmasters, $125,000 for Alpine APL Pipers, $75,000 for American Gambits and $50,000 for CheQ Mumba Masters; the champions also received a reported $50,000 bonus, alongside their share of the performance pool.The third-place finish gave the franchise a strong result in the season that followed Piqué’s arrival, although it does not establish the financial return on his investment. The team also featured in The Untold Story of FYERS American Gambits, a documentary released on ZEE5.Piqué’s chess portfolio now spans two ventures, with American Gambits adding a team-franchise investment to his earlier involvement in Freestyle Chess. The exact terms remain private, but his move reflects a broader shift among sporting figures who see chess not only as competition, but as a property with room to grow through media, new formats and global audiences.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Business as usual for victorious Man City despite lingering state of limbo
articles.summary: Man City 3-2 Ipswich: Erling Haaland’s brace and a first goal of 2026 for Phil Foden extended City’s lead at the top of the table to six points
articles.body:
Business as usual for Manchester City . Or should that be business as unusual? City may be in a strange kind of limbo but their new normal looked distinctly similar to the old variant. They won. Whatever punishments may await in the wake of the 114 guilty verdicts, which City are appealing, for now they are constructing a title challenge which, perhaps, the Premier League could do without. They are leaders with a six-point advantage at the summit and, some would say, an asterisk or two.

But Enzo Maresca 's stellar start has given him outright possession of a record. The Italian has seven victories out of seven in the top flight, the longest winning start to a reign in the Premier League. Beating Ipswich took him past Carlo Ancelotti, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and his predecessor Pep Guardiola , all tied on six. "For sure I didn't expect to win seven games out of seven," said Maresca. "It's a matter of winning games in this business." It has been at City, anyway.

So life in the wake of the independent commission's damning conclusions rather resembled the time before it. There was the statutory Erling Haaland goal, as he scored a second successive brace. The Norwegian has 12 goals in his last eight outings for City. A weakened City team had a talisman in attack ensuring that Ipswich's competitiveness did not earn them a point. Even when Maresca's policy of picking Haaland seemed to backfire, after he hobbled off at the end , the Norwegian could reassure his manager. "He said he was okay so hopefully it is nothing serious," said the Italian.

If so, Haaland was not the only City forward with reasons to enjoy the day. Outside the Etihad Stadium, they did a roaring trade in inflatable bananas. Some are manufactured by their old striker Imre Varadi, the man nicknamed "Imre Banana" in his playing days. If commercial deals involving City have come under the microscope of late, this one will benefit a man who scored goals for them in the second tier in the 1980s.

Maresca's children were among those trying to buy bananas – "I will ask them now," he said, waiting to hear if they succeeded – and, in their somewhat surreal way, the bananas form part of the City fans' response to a ruling that could bring all this to an end. Call it gallows humour or defiance but fans chanted "Stockport away", envisaging a rather different fixture list. When Jeremy Doku was fouled, they chorused "same old City, always cheating".

Otherwise, however, it had the air of another of City's Saturday 3pm kick-offs, just as the Paris Saint-Germain game felt like a big Champions League game. In the interim, anyway, the guilty verdicts may not have changed much.

There was one significant difference, however: Phil Foden ended a 35-game goal drought for City with a belated first strike of 2026. The local marked his first appearance since his Manchester derby red card by slotting home after Doku's cutback. Maresca, who had predicted Foden would score, looked prophetic. "He's one of the best Premier League players and it's my duty to help him be one of the best players," said the manager.

Foden owed his presence to a wholesale policy of rotation after City's considerable efforts against PSG. Maresca made six changes, giving Ayyoub Bouaddi a first Premier League start. With Enzo Fernandez and Elliot Anderson held in reserve, City's bench cost more than the starters, around £500m. The Argentinian was summoned earlier than expected when Mateo Kovacic, who had been excellent, hobbled off. While five City players sustained problems, Maresca was most concerned about the substitute Antoine Semenyo. "The only one we need to wait on is Antoine," his manager said.

Kovacic had made City's second goal as Haaland struck for an eighth game in a row, heading in after a lovely bit of skill and a deft chipped cross from Kovacic. Iliman Ndiaye was the provider of the Norwegian's first goal against Paris Saint-Germain with a cross for a towering header. This was a different kind of assist, with a perceptive pass, followed by two terrific Haaland touches, the second dispatched beyond Christian Walton. Briefly it seemed that Haaland had his ninth Premier League hat-trick, hooking in a volley after Ndiaye had hit the bar, but Fernandez was offside.

Instead, it brought Ipswich back into the game. They had levelled when Daizen Maeda scored his first goal for Ipswich after darting in behind Marc Guehi. It was not Guehi's finest day: he fouled the Ipswich substitute Azor Matusiwa for a late penalty that Zian Flemming converted. City have now conceded nine goals in their last three home matches in all competitions and the last few minutes were fraught.

"I am disappointed we haven't taken points," said Ipswich manager Gary O'Neil. His team had begun well organised in a 5-4-1 formation he has used against City before and ended on the front foot. They looked a side who will be in the Premier League next year. Will City?

articles.title: Iraola hails Fulham players and supporters after first win
articles.summary: Alvaro Arbeloa hailed Fulham’s character after they secured a 1-0 win over Hull City for their first Premier League victory of the season.The Fulham boss was...
articles.body:
Alvaro Arbeloa hailed Fulham's character after they secured a 1-0 win over Hull City for their first Premier League victory of the season.

The Fulham boss was delighted with the way his side continued to attack after taking the lead through Alex Iwobi and believes the victory was reward for their recent work.

"I'm so proud of my players because they played with great personality, great character," Arbeloa said.

"We scored one goal, and we continued attacking in the second half."

Arbeloa was also pleased for the Fulham supporters after seeing his side return to winning ways.

"I'm so happy for our supporters – they deserve this victory, this win," he said.

The Spaniard also praised the squad for continuing to trust in his approach despite pressure building on his position following a poor start.

"It's not easy for players when you are working hard, when you are doing what your coach is asking you, and you don't win games," Arbeloa said.

"It's not easy to keep doing the same things, keep working, keep trying to improve.

"And my players believe in our ideas, and they play in the way that we are playing, even when we were losing games."

articles.title: Gianni Infantino reportedly received $1.72 million in undisclosed World Cup compensation
articles.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino reportedly received an additional $1.7 million in 2024 through a U.S. entity connected to the 2026 World Cup. The payment, wh...
articles.body:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino is facing renewed scrutiny after U.S. tax filings reportedly showed that a World Cup-related entity paid him an additional $1.72 million in 2024. The payment was not listed in FIFA's public compensation disclosure for that year, according to reporting by ESPN.

The report has raised questions about how FIFA discloses compensation paid through separate entities. However, the reported omission does not by itself establish that Infantino or FIFA violated any law or organizational rule.

FIFA has rejected allegations that it failed to disclose financial information or breached its statutes. The organization says its compensation reporting complies with applicable requirements and that an independent subcommittee determines the president's annual compensation and other contractual benefits.

What the financial filings reportedly show

Reporting published on Oct. 13, 2026, said U.S. tax filings showed that FWC2026 US Inc. paid Infantino approximately $1.72 million in 2024. The nonprofit entity was established to help manage the U.S. side of the 2026 World Cup.

ESPN's report identified the payment in FWC2026 US Inc.'s IRS filing, while FIFA's public compensation disclosure did not list it separately. FIFA says it complies with all reporting requirements and rejects any suggestion that it violated its statutes. Whether the payment should have been disclosed differently remains a question of reporting rules and documentation.

Tax filings and annual reports serve different purposes, so the documents need to be assessed together. The central issue is whether compensation paid through a separate tournament entity was adequately disclosed under FIFA's rules and reporting practices.

FIFA's 2024 financial disclosure listed Infantino's base salary at 2.6 million Swiss francs. It also reported 1.65 million francs in variable compensation and 24,000 francs in allowances, before personal taxes.

The reported $1.72 million payment from FWC2026 would be additional to the compensation disclosed by FIFA. However, the amounts should not be combined without accounting for currency differences, reporting categories and the distinction between payments made by separate entities.

FIFA's 2025 compensation report listed a base salary of 2.6 million Swiss francs, variable compensation of 2.2 million francs and allowances of 24,000 francs. FIFA said the variable compensation would be paid in 2026. These figures should be kept separate from the reported 2024 payment unless the underlying records establish their relationship.

FIFA says it publishes annual compensation for senior officials, including its president. This policy aims to show the public how its top leaders are paid.

The reported payment raises questions about whether compensation from a separate World Cup entity should also have been disclosed. The omission does not prove a legal violation, but it raises concerns about transparency.

Former FIFA governance committee chairman Miguel Maduro reportedly called for scrutiny. His comments reflect his interpretation of FIFA's rules, not a legal finding. Any conclusion would require reviewing the relevant rules, contracts and explanations from FIFA and FWC2026.

What role FWC2026 plays in the tournament

FWC2026 US Inc. was established to support the organization and operation of the 2026 World Cup in the United States. The tournament was jointly hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico and concluded in July 2026.

FIFA and its affiliated entities handle different aspects of tournament operations. Consequently, financial information may appear in separate records. Comparing those records can help journalists and the public understand payments that may not be obvious from a single annual report.

The key questions are why the payment was made, which responsibilities it covered, who approved it and how FIFA believes it should be disclosed. The available reporting has raised those questions, but a complete explanation depends on the underlying agreements and financial records.

The wider scrutiny facing FIFA leadership

Infantino's leadership remains under scrutiny following the collapse of FIFA Forward Enterprise, a proposal to create a company to manage the commercial interests of FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, and to sell a minority stake to private investors. The proposal was abandoned in July 2026 after opposition from football leaders.

On October 15, Infantino apologized to the FIFA Council for mistakes in communication and consultation regarding the proposal. English and German football leaders nevertheless continued to question his leadership.

Infantino has led FIFA since 2016 and was re-elected in 2023 for a term ending in 2027. On October 8, Reuters reported that all 54 African member associations had pledged support for his re-election in March 2027.

One unresolved issue is how FIFA accounts for the reported FWC2026 payment under its compensation disclosure policy. The U.S. filing provides evidence of a payment, while FIFA disputes claims that it failed to meet its disclosure obligations.

It is also important to distinguish documented information from reports about possible payments in 2025 or 2026. Those claims require supporting records before specific amounts, dates or arrangements can be presented as established facts.

Further documentation could clarify the payment's purpose, approval process and disclosure treatment. Until those details are established, the report raises legitimate questions about transparency but should not be described as proof of misconduct or a confirmed rule violation.

Why the story matters after the 2026 World Cup

The 2026 World Cup has concluded, but questions about FIFA's finances remain relevant beyond the tournament itself. The organization oversees international competitions and distributes funds that affect national associations, clubs and football development programs around the world.

Clear compensation disclosures help the public understand how senior officials are paid. When payments involve more than one entity, consistent explanations become especially important. They allow readers to distinguish ordinary contractual arrangements from potential reporting gaps that may require further scrutiny.

The reported $1.72 million payment has drawn renewed attention to FIFA's disclosure practices. FIFA has denied wrongdoing, and the available reporting does not independently establish a violation. Further records and clear explanations from the parties involved would help resolve the remaining questions.

Fun fact: Gianni Infantino was named an honorary citizenship of Reggio Calabria, Italy, in 2025 because Infantino frequently visited the city as a child.

articles.title: Boos and bananas on day of defiance at Man City
articles.summary: Manchester City fans boo the Premier League anthem before watching their side move six points clear at the top of the table.
articles.body:
It started with Manchester City supporters booing the Premier League anthem and ended with Phil Foden taking an inflatable banana into his Match of the Day interview after helping see off Ipswich to pull six points clear at the top of the table.

On a day of defiance in east Manchester, City's fans made their feelings crystal clear in their first top-flight home game since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules .

Tens of thousands inside Etihad Stadium booed and jeered when the Premier League anthem was played over the speakers shortly before kick-off, then they started chanting 'City, City, City'.

There was a chant about playing Stockport away and the gallows humour continued when City fans sang 'You're going down with the City' to Ipswich's travelling support.

City boss Enzo Maresca, who is the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge, said afterwards he felt the air of defiance from the stands even before kick-off.

"The environment was very good," said the Italian after a game watched by 60,817, a new record crowd at Etihad Stadium.

"The fans, the club and the players are all together on this journey."

City fans arrived at the ground to find hundreds of inflatable bananas had been placed on seats in the home sections for fans to wave throughout the game.

They were visible in the away end at Liverpool last week but this was on a different scale and the Etihad was turned into a sea of yellow.

The inflatables are a flashback to the late '80s when what began as a light-hearted joke soon turned into one of the most memorable fan crazes in English football.

They are enjoying a revival at a time when City have appealed after being found guilty of charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, and creating 'sham contracts' to inflate sponsorship deals by £830m.

There were surreal scenes at one point on Saturday as fans jeered during the Premier League anthem while waving the inflatables in the air.

"You can tell they are behind us and they're pushing us," Phil Foden said when asked about the fans after scoring on his return to the side following suspension after being sent off against Manchester United on 13 September.

Foden's 19th-minute opener was his first goal of 2026.

"It's nice to play at home and you can hear how loud they are," he added. "They're giving us that extra boost that we need."

'I didn't expect to win seven out of seven'

Taking over from Pep Guardiola - 20 trophies during 10 seasons in charge - was always going to be a big challenge for Maresca.

Seven matches in, City's Premier League record remains flawless.

No points dropped, seven wins out of seven despite falling behind against Bournemouth and playing for more than an hour with 10 men at Manchester United.

"For sure I didn't expect to win seven out of seven," said Maresca. "We are working well and working good.

"I'm very happy especially with the situation in general.

"Today we controlled the game for 95 minutes. We created chances, we scored.

"We finished with a little bit of suffering together but overall, it is good."

On Foden's impressive return to action, Maresca added: "I said since day one that I love Phil. I know him from years ago and I know how good he is.

"It's a matter of helping him to again be one of the best players in the Premier League."

Despite the off-field turmoil, this is City's best start to a league season in 129 years.

Only Chelsea in 2005-06 (first nine) and Liverpool in 2019-20 (first eight) have ever won the first seven matches of a Premier League campaign.

"First of all, I am very happy because it's a matter of winning games in this business," said Maresca after the game.

"We were able to win seven in a row and what made me very happy was day by day with the players, the way they are working and how I can see them improving.

"Today I thought we controlled the game, created chances and [were] good off the ball. We are doing well and I think that's the most important thing."

On his players dealing with the events surrounding the club off the field, Maresca said: "They are not worried about people who judge from outside because they know people are trying to judge them.

"Inside, I promise the players are happy. They're getting credit and I give credit to them."
authors: Neil Johnston - BBC Sport football reporter

articles.title: Rangers Midfielder Wanted Again By Beşiktaş: Should McInnes Sell Him In January?
articles.summary: Four times now. That’s how often a Turkish giant has come knocking for one of Derek McInnes‘s most prized midfielders, and four times the move has fallen apa...
articles.body:
Four times now. That's how often a Turkish giant has come knocking for one of Derek McInnes 's most prized midfielders, and four times the move has fallen apart.

Takvim, relayed via Sport Witness , says Beşiktaş still haven't given up. The Istanbul club plans to return in January, and they're casting the net wider this time, with West Ham defender Konstantinos Mavropanos also sitting on their shortlist.

Nicolas Raskin is the man at the heart of it. The 25-year-old Belgian international arrived from Standard Liège in January 2023 for a modest fee and has since become the engine of the Ibrox midfield. His contract runs until 2028, and a €15m price tag keeps cropping up in the chatter.

Closer than most fans realised. Late in the summer window, reports claimed Beşiktaş had a deal sorted, and Raskin appeared set to fly out. Then he turned up in the squad for the Falkirk game, played 90 minutes and rejected the offer.

He admitted afterwards he'd been mentally ready to go, yet he also called the matter closed. That door hasn't slammed shut for good, though.

GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – OCTOBER 10: Nicolas Raskin of Rangers is seen warming up during the William Hill Premiership 2026/27 match between Glasgow Rangers and Kilmarnock at Ibrox Stadium on October 10, 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

If I'm McInnes, I say no unless the money's silly. Raskin is the one midfielder I can't easily replace. He carries the ball out of tight spaces, he wins second balls, and he already knows exactly what I want from him. Selling midseason means hunting for a like-for-like option while rival clubs charge a premium for desperation. That rarely ends well.

Then there's the head issue. Raskin has said he was ready to leave, and a player with one foot out of the door can drift. I'd sit him down, tell him straight what the plan is, and watch his training closely. If his standards slip, the decision makes itself.

The €15m figure isn't bad for a player who cost a modest fee, yet it's no fortune either. A bigger league might offer more come summer, and Beşiktaş can't match that stage. I'd tell the board to hold firm and only talk if a Premier League or Serie A club turns up. Otherwise, he stays, and I keep the engine running.

articles.title: Erling Haaland injury update: Man City star 'OK' after limping off vs Ipswich
articles.summary: Manchester City star Erling Haaland said he was "OK" after limping heavily at the end of Saturday's win at Ipswich.
articles.body:
Manchester City star Erling Haaland said he was "OK" after limping heavily at the end of Saturday's 3-2 win over Ipswich, per head coach Enzo Maresca.

Haaland went straight down the tunnel after the final whistle at the Etihad Stadium, sparking fears that the Norway star had suffered an injury.

The striker scored twice in the Oct. 17 victory, but Maresca said after the game that he was one of several City players who ended the match carrying some form of injury concern.

Aside from Haaland, the coach named Antoine Semenyo, Matheus Nunes, Nico O'Reilly and Mateo Kovacic as players who did not exit the match unscathed.

"We will see," Maresca said in his post-match news conference. "Unfortunately in 10 minutes we had four or five players … Matheus, Kova, Erling, Antoine and Nico also … they are inside now but we will see, I don't know, I don't have any news at the moment."

Best Premier League action, scenes and drama from 2026-27 season

Maresca added that three players, including Haaland, had assured him that they were OK, with his main concern over the status of Semenyo.

"I asked all of them. Mateo said he was OK, Matheus said he was OK, Erling also said that he was OK," Maresca said. "Nico still has the same problem in his back that (he suffered) in the warm-up against Coventry. The only one we need to wait a little bit (for) is Antoine, and we will see."

Asked if Haaland had a knee injury, Maresca replied: "I don't know, I asked him and he said he was OK so hopefully it is nothing serious."

Haaland's brace took him to eight Premier League goals on the season, putting him three goals ahead in the Golden Boot race.

City is next in action in just three days, as it plays host to AEK Athens in the Champions League on Tuesday, Oct. 20.

Even before the Ipswich match, Maresca said he would likely need to give Haaland and other stars a rest at some point soon.

"At some point we probably need to give him rest, some days off," the City boss said of Haaland during his pre-game news conference.

"We are thinking about this not just with Erling because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams.

"Elliot (Anderson), Enzo (Fernandez), Marc (Guehi), Erling, Rúben (Dias) – so at some point we probably need to give them some rest."

articles.title: 😎 Bayern Munich hit six and go top of the Bundesliga
articles.summary: Bayern Munich thrashed RB Leipzig 6-1 on Saturday (17) to go top of the Bundesliga.Luis Díaz (three), Pavlovic, Olise and Harry Kane scored the goals at the...
articles.body:
Bayern Munich thrashed RB Leipzig 6-1 on Saturday (17) to go top of the Bundesliga.

Luis Díaz (three), Pavlovic, Olise and Harry Kane scored the goals at the Allianz Arena.

Bayern moved onto 14 points, overtaking Borussia Dortmund, who also have 14 points but an inferior goal difference.

To stay top, however, Bayern will need Freiburg to slip up. Freiburg have 13 points and visit Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday (18).

And the next round of Bundesliga fixtures will see Freiburg host Bayern Munich on Sunday the 25th at 1:30 p.m.

Before that, Bayern will turn their attention to the Champions League. They host Arsenal in a blockbuster clash at 4 p.m. on Wednesday (21).

Bayern Munich opened the scoring in the 12th minute. Luis Díaz latched onto Kimmich's ball in behind the defense and finished with class to make it 1-0.

Luis Díaz then turned provider, finding Pavlovic in the box to double the lead. Still in the first half, Olise made it 3-0 from a Harry Kane assist.

Bayern kept up the pace, turning the victory into a rout in the second half. Luis Díaz scored twice more, while Harry Kane also got on the scoresheet.

Maksimovic scored a fine consolation goal for RB Leipzig in stoppage time.

articles.title: El Barça se lleva la 'batalla' de La Cartuja
articles.standfirst: Mucha tensión, muchos goles y mucha polémica en una nueva victoria del Barça que se decantó tras la expulsión de Facundo Bernal en el minuto 54. Nueve de nueve para el líder
articles.summary: Mucha tensión, muchos goles y mucha polémica en una nueva victoria del Barça que se decantó tras la expulsión de Facundo Bernal en el minuto 54. Nueve de nueve para el líder
articles.body: El Betis tampoco pudo con este intratable Barça que ha ganado los 12 partidos oficiales que ha disputado. Como era de esperar, hubo de todo en un partido en el que se medían dos equipos en un gran momento de juego. Mucha tensión, muchos goles, mucha polémica y una expulsión que decantó definitivamente el choque para los de Flick. Los béticos se quejan sobre todo de un tanto anulado a Lo Celso, que hubiera supuesto el 2-2 por una mano previa mucho antes del gol. Lamine volvió a marcar diferencias aunque abandonó La Cartuja entre abucheos por ser protagonista en la expulsión de Facundo Bernal. El choque más complicado hasta la fecha para los de Flick empezó a decidirse antes del minuto 10 cuando Lamine Yamal se inventó un golazo para acabar con las esperanzas béticas. Recibe un balón en banda, se va de Facundo Bernal con un recorte y lanza un zurdazo teledirigido a la escuadra de Valles. El Betis no se dio por vencido y llegó a empatar por medio de Valentín Gómez, pero Rodri antes del descanso y luego Gabriel Jesus y Eric García dieron la ventaja definitiva al líder. Los de Pellegrini llegaron a empatar con un golazo de Lo Celso, pero fue anulado vía VAR por una mano clara del Cucho Hernández en el inicio de la jugada. La polémica está servida con la interpretación de la norma arbitral. Cada uno la ve según lo que le interesa, lo de siempre. La expulsión de Facundo Bernal acabó por hundir al Betis con media hora de juego por disputarse. El inicio inmaculado de los de Flick podía verse frenado en una semana infernal en lo futbolístico con visitas a Betis y PSG y cierre de órdago en el Camp Nou frente al Real Madrid. La primera piedra era un Betis de Champions que no perdía en La Cartuja en LaLiga desde el 6 de diciembre de 2025, curiosamente ante el Barça por un 3-5, en un total de 15 partidos. Y la prueba fue superada con polémica y con éxito. Flick no especuló y sacó un equipo más que titular mientras que Pellegrini reservó a algunas piezas importantes como Isco, Natan, Deossa o Antony. La posesión del balón fue desde el principio para el Barça y el dominio se transformó en ventaja pronto con el golazo de Lamine por toda la escuadra. Por el otro lado era Abde quien concentraba todo el peligro local. El partido estaba en lo quisieran los dos que llevaban el 10. Y de un córner provocado por el marroquí llegó el empate después de que un despeje llegara a los pies de Fornals, que puso un balón medido a la cabeza de Valentín Gómez. El partido se abrió, la especulación no tenía hueco en La Cartuja. Adeyemi tuvo el 1-2 tras un gran pase de Lamine, pero Valles le ganó el mano a mano, luego fue Bellerín quien tuvo el 2-1 a pase de Fornals, pero Joan García se lució. Los últimos minutos de la primera parte fueron trepidantes. Rodri consiguió el 1-2 al rematar de cabeza un córner sacado por Fermín y en el que Valles se quedó a media salida. El Betis no se vino abajo y Lo Celso empató sólo unos minutos después con un gran disparo desde fuera del área. Con la grada aún como loca en la celebración del segundo empate, el VAR avisó a Ricardo de Burgos de una mano previa en la jugada del Cucho Hernández y el golazo fue anulado para desesperación de todo el equipo bético con amarillas incluidas para Diego Llorente y el técnico Pellegrini. El inicio azulgrana de la segunda parte fue como el de Estambul en Champions. A los 30 segundos pudo marcar Gabriel Jesus a pase de Adeyemi, luego fue Fermín el que obligó a hacer un paradón a Valles. Gabriel Jesus llegó a marcar a pase de Lamine, pero fue anulado por fuera de juego. El brasileño repitió con la red un minuto después a pase de Lamine para el 1-3. El Betis protestó una falta previa de Fermín. Sin tiempo para digerir el 1-3, llegó el 2-3 cuando Abde culminó una contra en la que el Barça pidió falta sobre Fermín. Y ahí se lió cuando Valles levantó de mala manera a Fermín, que estaba en el suelo, se metió por medio Lamine para ayudar a su compañero y Facundo Bernal acabó el rifi-rafe general con un toque de cabezas con Lamine que le valió la expulsión. Con uno menos, el Betis se quedaba sin argumentos y el Barça le castigó enseguida con el cuarto gol obra de Eric García de cabeza tras un pase también de cabeza de Cubarsí. Ese gol, que todo el mundo vio que era la sentencia definitiva del partido, aplacó los ánimos y los últimos 20 minutos parecían de otro partido. Los dos técnicos fueron dando descanso a jugadores importantes pensando en la Champions y Flick dio unos minutos a Raphinha, que reaparecía tras su lesión con Brasil. Hubo tiempo para que Dani Olmo hiciera el quinto con un disparo desde fuera del área. Eric García se tuvo que retirar lesionado, la peor noticia para los catalanes. No hay quien pueda con este Barça. PSG y Real Madrid no se lo pondrán nada fácil en unos días.
